subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Catherine of Braganza
description: A fast breakdown of Catherine of Braganza for builders.

hook.text: When Portuguese princess Catherine married England's Charles II in 1662, she brought a chest of tea.

buildup.text: Catherine made tea fashionable at the English court. Nobles copied the queen's afternoon ritual.

discovery.text: Before Catherine, England barely knew tea. Within decades, it became the national drink.

twist.text: Her dowry also included Bombay (Mumbai) and Tangier—but tea had the most lasting cultural impact.

climax.text: A single queen's preference reshaped an entire nation's drinking habits for centuries to come.

punchline.text: A queen's dowry included cities. Tea mattered more.

quiz.question: Who introduced tea to the English royal court?

details.summary: Catherine of Braganza, a Portuguese princess, married King Charles II of England in 1662 and brought her tea-drinking habit to the English court. She popularized tea among the aristocracy, making it fashionable.
details.whyItMatters: A single royal marriage shifted an entire nation's beverage preferences. Catherine's influence shows how cultural change can start at the top and cascade down.
takeaways: Catherine of Braganza married Charles II of England in 1662
She brought her Portuguese tea-drinking habit to court
Her influence made tea fashionable among English aristocracy

faq.question: Was Catherine really responsible for Britain's love of tea?
faq.answer: She was a key catalyst but not the sole cause. Tea was already available in England. Catherine made it courtly and fashionable, but the East India Company's cheap imports, sugar availability, and domestic marketing later made tea accessible to all classes.

faq.question: What was Catherine's tea-drinking practice like?
faq.answer: Catherine drank Chinese tea at court, likely green tea served without milk in the Chinese fashion. Courtiers adopted the habit to mirror the queen. Tea parties became fashionable social events. Within a generation, tea had spread from the court to the wealthy merchant class.
